title: Graduate survey: status twelve months after graduation
bodyMd: A university surveyed 400 of its graduates twelve months after graduation. Each respondent reported exactly one status: employed, in further study, or seeking work. The table gives the counts by degree programme.

data.caption: Status of 400 surveyed graduates twelve months after graduation, by programme.

accessibilityText: A table with five rows and five columns. Economics: 160 respondents, 120 employed, 24 in further study, 16 seeking work. Engineering: 120 respondents, 96 employed, 18 further study, 6 seeking. Humanities: 80 respondents, 44 employed, 24 further study, 12 seeking. Law: 40 respondents, 26 employed, 10 further study, 4 seeking. Total: 400 respondents, 286 employed, 76 further study, 38 seeking work.

provenance.notes: Invented data for a fictional survey, written for this item set. Each row sums to its respondents, and the counts were chosen so that conditional shares resolve by hand. Not derived from any real dataset or published test item.
